first_visit.nexus_prime: First visit to Nexus Prime. The docking fee alone cost more than fuel at most stations. The old Aurelia's hull loomed above the bay, polished to a museum shine nobody stopped to look at. Holographic price tickers scrolled across every surface. The air tasted stale and filtered.
first_visit.stellaris_port: Arrived at Stellaris Port. Crystal chandeliers threw fragmented light across the promenade, but past the polish I saw the prices. A cup of coffee cost what a miner made in a shift.
first_visit.breakstone: Arrived at Breakstone. Rock dust on everything: the handrails, the meal trays, the inside of anyone's lungs if they stayed long enough. The station thrummed with a rhythm that never stopped: drilling, hauling, drilling again. Someone had chalked a name and two dates on the corridor wall near Bay 3. Nobody had erased it.
first_visit.iron_depths: First visit to Iron Depths. The station groans under pressure shifts you can feel in your teeth. Fluorescent lights flicker in the deeper corridors and nobody fixes them. DCMC logos on every surface, but the faces underneath tell a different story than the quarterly reports.
first_visit.forgeworks: Docked at Forgeworks. The heat hits before the airlock finishes cycling. The air tastes like ozone and ambition and the sweat of people working twelve-hour shifts in thermal suits. Foundry sparks arc overhead like brief, doomed stars. Guild inspectors and Union foremen eye each other across the canteen and neither blinks first.
first_visit.axiom_labs: Arrived at Axiom Labs. Synthesized coffee. Color-coded lab coats crowded every corridor, arguing in shorthand. The Okafor Institute's reputation preceded it.
first_visit.nova_research: First visit to Nova Research. Three badge checks before I reached the public concourse. The corridors were soundproofed and the researchers walked fast with their eyes on their slates. The cafeteria served three meals.
first_visit.havens_rest: Arrived at Haven's Rest. The air smelled like soil and basil. Real basil, not the synthesized kind. Children running between planting beds. Wind chimes made from recycled hull plating.
first_visit.verdant: Docked at Verdant. Rows of green stretched through observation windows as far as I could see. The light was too even, too perfect, the grow-lamps mimicking a sun that never existed here.
first_visit.crimson_reach: Arrived at Crimson Reach. Dim lighting, exposed pipes, and the smell of coolant. Half the overhead panels were dark. The other half flickered on a schedule nobody had posted. A woman at the bar watched me dock through a porthole, then looked away. No questions asked here.
first_visit.the_fulcrum: First visit to The Fulcrum. The corridors were sterile. Not clean. Sterile, like something had been scrubbed away. Military-grade scanners at every junction, guards who checked credentials without speaking, blast doors sealed on sections nobody acknowledged. The air recyclers worked perfectly.
